documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly physical.

Alcohol: went to the counseling program intake and about three group sessions in January, then stopped going — schedule clashed with second shift coverage. Still drinking most days, "less than before" by his estimate. Not interested in the medication right now. We left the door open.
Achalasia: swallowing fine. GI never did send the dilation note; he says they want to see him yearly.
Diabetes, HTN, lipids: meds as before (metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20). No side effects.

Exam: vitals as charted. Weight about 98 kg, holding. HEENT normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, liver edge just palpable, nontender. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable. No edema. PHQ-2 1. AUDIT-C 9.

Plan: CMP, A1c, lipids today. Continue meds. Revisit counseling options at each visit. RTC 3 months for follow-up.

events.reason: Fatigue, shortness of breath on exertion, sore tongue

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, winded, sore tongue.

HPI: Seen to follow up the achalasia and the drinking, but he has a new complaint. For about two months he has been worn out by mid-shift and short of breath going up the stairs to the mezzanine office, which never bothered him before. Tongue has been sore and looks red; spicy food burns. No chest pain, no palpitations, no black or bloody stools, no vomiting. Swallowing still fine since the dilation.
Diet: honest that it's mostly fast food or nothing during the day.
Alcohol: six to eight cans of beer a day lately.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20.

Exam: pale conjunctivae and palms. Tongue smooth and beefy red, papillae lost. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Neuro: sensation and gait normal.

Labs drawn here this morning. CBC back at 1 pm: hemoglobin 9.2, MCV 115. Retic 1%.

A/P
1. Macrocytic anemia with glossitis in a heavy drinker with a poor diet: folate deficiency at the top of the list, B12 also possible (on metformin). Folate, B12 and methylmalonic acid pending. Will call with results and start replacement. ED for chest pain, fainting or worse breathlessness.
2. Alcohol use disorder: drinking more. Reoffered counseling and medication; he'll think about it.
3. Achalasia: stable.
4. HTN, T2DM: continue.

documents.title: Anemia results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with results. Folate 2 (low), B12 400 (normal), methylmalonic acid normal. Together with Hgb 9.2, MCV 115, retic 1%: folate deficiency anemia, from diet and alcohol.
Started folic acid 1 mg daily, sent to pharmacy. Explained that drinking blocks folate and that the anemia will come back if the drinking and diet don't change. He heard that. Recheck CBC in about 3 months. Feeling the same, no chest pain.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Upton on 08/15/2024 for follow-up of achalasia, one year after pneumatic balloon dilation (08/09/2023). He reports eating a normal diet with only rare, brief hesitation. No regurgitation, no chest pain, weight stable. Exam unremarkable. Symptoms remain well controlled. I will see him annually or sooner if dysphagia returns.
Medications per our record: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Gastroenterology

documents.body: Darren — your blood count is back up to 13.7 (it was 9.2 in June) and the red cell size is nearly normal. The anemia has resolved on the folic acid. Finish out the folic acid through early October and then we'll stop it.

documents.title: Hypertension Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 53 y/o here to go over blood pressure after finishing the six monthly nurse check-ins. Taking lisinopril every morning, says he hasn't missed. More active since the winter — stairs at work, walks on weekends. Still frustrated: "I'm doing everything and it's still not where you want it."
Nurse visit readings Sep→Feb: 150/92, 148/90, 145/88, 142/86, 140/84, 138/82.
Other problems: obesity, achalasia (stable after dilation), alcohol use disorder, folate deficiency anemia last year (resolved). Alcohol: still daily, didn't want to quantify today.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.

O: BP 136/80. BMI 30. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Exam otherwise unremarkable.

A/P
1. Essential hypertension: steady improvement with lifestyle changes over six months. Pointed that out to him — 14 points systolic is real progress. Continue lisinopril 20. Home readings, send me a week's worth in a month.
2. T2DM, lipids: labs today. Continue metformin and atorvastatin.
3. AUD: offered resources again.
4. Anemia: CBC with today's labs.
Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Switching to mail order
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Work changed our plan, now they want 90 day mail order for everything. Can you send all three there? Mail order info is on the card I uploaded.

documents.title: RE: Switching to mail order
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Sent metformin, lisinopril and atorvastatin to the mail-order pharmacy, 90 days with refills. First shipment usually takes about 10 days, so let us know if you run short at the local pharmacy before then.
